plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Genovese'
plants.tip: Pinch out the growing tip once it has four leaf pairs. Flower buds turn the remaining leaves bitter.
plants.colour: Large cupped mid-green leaves

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Nufar'
plants.tip: Bred for fusarium resistance, so it is the one to use if a previous basil wilted and died in the same compost.
plants.colour: Broad flat glossy green leaves

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Napoletano'
plants.tip: The blistered leaves hold water and rot in still, damp air. Give the plant space and some air movement.
plants.colour: Very large blistered pale-green leaves

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Italian Large Leaf'
plants.tip: Harvest whole stems back to a low leaf pair rather than picking single leaves, and it rebranches from there.
plants.colour: Large flat light-green leaves

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Mammoth'
plants.tip: The leaves are big enough to wrap food but wilt within an hour of cutting. Pick immediately before use.
plants.colour: Huge crinkled mid-green leaves

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Aroma 2'
plants.tip: Copes with a cool summer better than most Genovese types, but growth still stalls on a cold windowsill at night.
plants.colour: Deep green cupped leaves

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Eleonora'
plants.tip: Downy mildew shows as yellowing between the veins with grey fuzz beneath. This one resists it; wet leaves still invite it.
plants.colour: Mid-green domed leaves with a matt finish

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Dolce Fresca'
plants.tip: Compact enough for a windowsill pot. Cut it hard and often or the base goes woody by midsummer.
plants.colour: Small glossy mid-green leaves on a dense mound

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Prospera'
plants.tip: Downy mildew resistant, so it survives humid spells that flatten a standard Genovese. Water the compost, not the leaves.
plants.colour: Dark green cupped Genovese-type leaves

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Rutgers Devotion DMR'
plants.tip: Resists downy mildew without losing the sweet Genovese flavour. Sow in succession; one plant will not keep up.
plants.colour: Broad dark green leaves, lightly cupped

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Rutgers Obsession DMR'
plants.tip: Remove flower spikes the day you see them. Once it is allowed to bloom the leaf flavour drops away.
plants.colour: Mid-green cupped leaves, slightly pointed

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Amazel'
plants.tip: Sterile, so it sets no seed and never runs to flower. Feed it fortnightly because it keeps growing all season.
plants.colour: Large mid-green leaves on tall green stems

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Everleaf Emerald Towers'
plants.tip: Columnar and much slower to flower than Genovese. Let it grow upright and pick from the side shoots.
plants.colour: Dark green leaves on a narrow upright column

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Everleaf Thai Towers'
plants.tip: Slow to bolt for a Thai basil, so the aniseed flavour holds into late summer. Pick from the sides.
plants.colour: Green leaves with purple stems in an upright column

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum var. minimum (Greek bush basil)
plants.tip: Forms a tight dome on its own and needs no pinching for shape. Let the compost dry slightly between waterings.
plants.colour: Tiny bright green leaves in a tight dome

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Spicy Globe'
plants.tip: The small leaves dry out fast in a small pot. A wide, shallow container keeps the dome even.
plants.colour: Very small mid-green leaves in a dense ball

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Fino Verde'
plants.tip: The small leaves bruise far less than large-leaved basil, so cut whole sprigs for a garnish.
plants.colour: Small pointed light-green leaves

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Pluto'
plants.tip: A dwarf globe that suits a 12cm pot. It bolts quickly in heat, so keep it out of a closed conservatory.
plants.colour: Miniature dark-green leaves on a compact dome

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Minette'
plants.tip: Fine-leaved and dense. Pick sprigs rather than single leaves and the mound shape is kept.
plants.colour: Fine mid-green leaves in a low mound

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Dark Opal'
plants.tip: The purple fades towards green in poor light. Hours of direct sun are what keep the colour.
plants.colour: Deep purple-black leaves with pink flowers

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Purple Ruffles'
plants.tip: Slower and fussier than plain purple basil. Sow it warm and never let the compost sit cold and wet.
plants.colour: Frilled and fringed deep purple leaves

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Red Rubin'
plants.tip: Comes truer from seed than Dark Opal and holds its colour better. Pinch early to stop it going lanky.
plants.colour: Uniform burgundy-purple leaves

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Osmin Purple'
plants.tip: The darkest of the purple basils in full sun. In shade the leaves turn a muddy bronze instead.
plants.colour: Near-black purple leaves with a metallic sheen

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Amethyst Improved'
plants.tip: Thick down-curling leaves that shade the crown. Cut the flower spikes out to keep new leaves coming.
plants.colour: Thick down-curved leaves in deep matt purple

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Round Midnight'
plants.tip: Compact purple basil that stays neat in a pot. Colour tracks the hours of direct sun it gets.
plants.colour: Dark purple leaves on a compact rounded plant

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Green Ruffles'
plants.tip: The frilled leaves trap water and mark easily. Water at the compost and pick in the morning.
plants.colour: Crinkled and fringed apple-green leaves

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Cinnamon'
plants.tip: Grow it hot and bright; the scent thins in a dim, cool spot. Pinch the tips to keep it bushy.
plants.colour: Olive-green leaves with purple veins and stems

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Licorice' (anise basil)
plants.tip: Aniseed-scented, with stems that darken in sun. Pinch out the flower spikes to keep the leaves tender.
plants.colour: Green leaves flushed purple with dark purple stems

plants.name: Ocimum × africanum (lemon basil)
plants.tip: Bolts faster than sweet basil, so sow a fresh pot every three weeks through the summer.
plants.colour: Small pale-green leaves with white flowers

plants.name: Ocimum × africanum 'Sweet Dani'
plants.tip: A lemon basil selected for a strong citrus scent. It runs to flower quickly, so keep cutting the tips.
plants.colour: Light green narrow leaves with white flower spikes

plants.name: Ocimum × africanum 'Mrs Burns Lemon'
plants.tip: Larger-leaved and slower to bolt than common lemon basil. Cut it back by half after the first flush.
plants.colour: Bright green oval leaves with white flowers

plants.name: Ocimum × citriodorum 'Pesto Perpetuo'
plants.tip: It does not flower or set seed, so it keeps cropping. The cream margins scorch in hard afternoon sun.
plants.colour: Mid-green leaves with a clean cream margin

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Lime'
plants.tip: Short-lived and quick to bolt. Take cuttings in water or resow rather than nursing an old plant.
plants.colour: Small pale lime-green leaves

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Blue Spice'
plants.tip: Better as a scented pot plant than a cropping basil, as the leaves stay small. Let the bracts develop.
plants.colour: Grey-green leaves with purple flower bracts

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Christmas'
plants.tip: Fruity-scented, with flower bracts worth leaving on. Pinch the growing tips to keep the plant dense.
plants.colour: Glossy dark green leaves with deep purple flower bracts

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum var. thyrsiflora (Thai sweet basil)
plants.tip: The aniseed flavour survives a hot pan where sweet basil collapses. Grow it warmer than Genovese.
plants.colour: Narrow green leaves with purple stems and bracts

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Siam Queen'
plants.tip: Strong Thai basil with dense purple flower heads. Leave a few for the bees and cut the rest for leaf.
plants.colour: Dark green leaves with dense purple flower heads

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Cardinal'
plants.tip: Grown for the thick crimson flower bracts rather than the leaves, so let it bloom rather than pinching.
plants.colour: Green leaves beneath thick crimson flower bracts

plants.name: Ocimum basilicum 'Magical Michael'
plants.tip: An ornamental basil grown for its flower bracts. The leaves are edible but small, so crop it lightly.
plants.colour: Green leaves with white flowers in dark purple bracts

plants.name: Ocimum tenuiflorum (holy basil)
plants.tip: A short-lived perennial rather than an annual. Keep it above 10°C over winter and it runs a second year.
plants.colour: Slightly hairy green leaves with purple-tinged stems

plants.name: Ocimum tenuiflorum 'Rama'
plants.tip: Green-leaved tulsi with a clove scent. Pinch the flower spikes out to keep leaf production going.
plants.colour: Light green leaves with pale purple flower spikes

plants.name: Ocimum tenuiflorum 'Krishna'
plants.tip: Slower and smaller than the green tulsi, and it needs full sun to hold the purple in the leaf.
plants.colour: Purple-tinged green leaves with purple stems
